sections.title: THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS SOUTHERN TEXAS
sections.text: ...SUMMARY... Large to very large hail, damaging wind gusts, and a few tornadoes, are possible over parts of the lower Mississippi Valley/central Gulf Coast region today into this evening. Severe/damaging hail will be the main threat with thunderstorms over parts of south Texas.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: A low-amplitude trough is noted in mid-morning water vapor imagery translating eastward across the Plains. An embedded vorticity maxima/shortwave is noted within this trough moving across KS with a broad swath of subsidence overspreading the southern High Plains. Ascent associated with this feature is already overspreading the southern Plains/lower MS valley this morning with scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms noted across southeast OK in the vicinity of a diffuse surface low and ahead of a modest cold front. This activity is expected to increase in coverage and intensity through the afternoon as it propagates along a surface warm front draped to the east/southeast into the lower MS river valley. The surface cold front will continue to push into southern/southeast TX and will be the impetus for isolated thunderstorms this afternoon.

sections.title: Lower MS river valley
sections.text: A moist air mass is already in place across LA/southern MS this morning with dewpoints in the low 70s. Morning soundings show this moisture extends up to around 1 km with 7 C/km mid-level lapse rates. With temperatures already warming into the upper 70s amid broken low-level cumulus, any lingering inhibition will likely erode by early afternoon with widespread 2000-2500 J/kg MLCAPE values. 12 UTC soundings also show elongated hodographs with effective bulk shear values already near 40 knots. Increasing upper-level winds attendant to the shortwave will boost deep-layer shear further across the lower MS valley by mid afternoon. The kinematic profiles will support supercells, but storm motions along the warm frontal zone will likely favor a mix of quasi-discrete supercells to one or more clusters that may amalgamate into a more organized linear mode. Regardless, the favorable thermodynamic and kinematic environment will be supportive of damaging winds and large to very large hail - particularly across north-central LA into southwest MS where the potential for more discrete modes on the edge of the best instability is greatest. sections.title: South-central Texas
sections.text: Isolated thunderstorms are expected to develop along the surface cold front as it moves into south-central and southeast TX this afternoon. Mixed layer inhibition noted in 12 UTC RAOBs will likely linger through mid/late afternoon with gradual erosion due to morning stratus across the region. Glancing ascent from the passing wave to the north combined with lift along the front should be sufficient for a handful of elevated, isolated cells late this morning with higher probability for surface based convection this afternoon. Forecast soundings show straight, elongated hodographs favorable for supercell splits, and moderate instability combined with strong effective bulk shear will support the potential for large to very large hail as well as damaging winds. While confidence in this potential remains highest across the I-35 corridor in south-central TX, the environment is supportive of severe convection from the Rio Grande through east TX.

sections.title: Northern MS through central GA
sections.text: The severe hail/wind potential this morning will likely persist into the late evening and overnight hours across northern MS into central GA as the upper-level wave shifts into the southeastern CONUS. While lapse rates across this region are somewhat marginal in morning soundings, cooling aloft and strengthening upper-level winds associated with the approaching wave will support increasing instability and deep-layer shear through the day. Lift ahead of the wave and within a modest warm advection regime will support scattered thunderstorms this evening into the overnight hours. Sufficient boundary-layer moisture will be in place to support adequate MUCAPE within a sheared environment for a severe hail/wind risk. ..Moore/Hart.. 04/17/2022

sections.title: 20z update
sections.text: Strong/locally severe storms continue over northwest LA/southern AR in an area just north of a stationary front which extends from a weak surface low over east TX across northern LA/central MS and southern AL at 20z. Please refer to MCD 514 for the latest short-term details in this area. Otherwise, the general thunderstorm line was adjusted slightly based on latest observations and frontal movement. A small cluster of severe storms continues across central TX along the westward extension of the surface front. The downstream environment should continue support supercell storm structures capable of very large hail and possibly severe gusts given MLCAPE of around 2000 J/kg and 45-50 kts of deep-layer shear. Storms should move southeast towards the San Antonio area through early evening. Over the northeast FL peninsula, the Marginal Risk area was nudged south based on ongoing strong/severe storms along a sea-breeze boundary. Storms have a history of strong wind gusts and severe hail, and some localized severe risk will continue for a few more hours. Please see MCD 513 for the latest short-term thinking in this area. ..Bunting.. 04/17/2022 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1129 AM CDT Sun Apr

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A few strong to severe thunderstorms capable of large hail may affect parts of east-central Mississippi and west-central Alabama through the morning. It is unclear whether coverage of severe storms will warrant a severe thunderstorm watch.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A cluster of showers and thunderstorms over north-central MS includes a couple of intense cells with a history of hail. These storms are tracking east-southeastward at 25 knots, and will likely persist through the morning into central Alabama. The activity appears to be associated with a weak shortwave trough over AR/West TN, and in a region of modest elevated CAPE. Forecast soundings for this area show moderately steep mid-level lapse rates and sufficient deep layer shear for convective organization and occasional supercell structures. Present indications are that a few storms will continue to pose a risk of occasionally severe hail for a few hours. Coverage of strong storms is likely to be limited, and the need for a severe thunderstorm watch is uncertain. However, convective trends will be monitored. ..Hart.. 04/17/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storms are expected to form across the ArkLaTex area after 17Z, becoming increasingly severe as they travel across Louisiana and eventually southern Mississippi. Significant damaging hail will be possible, as well as severe gusts. A brief tornado may occur as well.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Scattered elevated convection is currently forming across northeast TX into southeast OK, ahead of a low-amplitude shortwave trough and within the 850 mb theta-e axis. This is within a weak pressure trough, but well north of the surface front which currently lies near Shreveport LA. Some of this activity may begin producing hail in the next 1-2 hours. Later this afternoon, and mainly after 18Z, convergence will increase near the boundary with a low developing near the Sabine Valley and into north-central LA. By this time, MLCAPE will have increased to over 2000 J/kg, and may approach 3000 J/kg by late afternoon. Ample boundary-layer moisture is in place, and heating will further deepen the moisture profile. Low-level southwesterly winds will not be very strong but will at least maintain the most unstable air up to the surface front. As storms develop east/southeast in the vicinity of the boundary and surface low, the strong instability and long hodographs (characterized by increasing speeds with height) will favor forward-tilted, southeastward-moving severe hail storms. Steep lapse rates aloft and long hodographs suggest a storm or two may produce wind-driven significant hail. If storm mode becomes more linear than expected, hail will still be possible but threat may trend toward damaging straight-line winds. Low-level SRH will not be strong as 850 mb winds only average 20 kt, but will be maximized near the boundary and support a brief tornado threat.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated thunderstorms are expected to develop in the coming hours along a cold front across south-central Texas. A favorable kinematic environment will support the potential for supercells with large to very large hail.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Latest GOES-16 visible imagery reveals the location of the surface cold front as it continues to push southeast into TX. A couple of weak thunderstorms have already initiated off this boundary, but have struggled to mature, quickly becoming displaced into the cool air to the north. The anemic nature to the prior convection is likely attributable to lingering mixed-layer inhibition, which is gradually diminishing as temperatures continue to slowly warm into the low to mid 80s where skies are mostly clear. Additional cumulus towers are noted along the front in latest visible and IR imagery, suggesting the probability for sustained thunderstorms continues to increase. Storms will likely intensify further in the coming hours as they move southeast into an air mass with richer boundary layer moisture (denoted by low 70s dewpoints). Parcel trajectories will likely deepen as cells encounter this air mass, allowing for better realization of the elongated wind profiles over the region. Nearly straight hodographs will support supercell structures with eventual storm splits. The combination of moderate instability and strong effective bulk wind shear (40-50 knots) will support the potential for severe hail (possibly up to 2 inches in diameter) and damaging winds. Trends will continue to be monitored, and a watch will likely be needed as soon as sufficient storm coverage becomes apparent.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Sporadic damaging winds and near-severe hail possible over the next couple of hours as thunderstorms continue to develop along sea-breeze boundaries in north-central Florida.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Thunderstorms developing along sea-breeze boundaries across north-central Florida have a history of producing sub-severe wind and hail over the past hour, with a notable 54 mph wind gust observed near Jacksonville, FL. Latest RAP analysis and forecast soundings hint that deep-layer flow is fairly weak, and this is confirmed by regional VWP observations. As such, the potential for sustained organized convection appears very minimal. However, these storms are developing in an environment with nearly 2000 J/kg SBCAPE, which may support a brief window for near-severe hail with initial updraft pulses. Additionally, lapse rates in the lowest 2-3 km are near 8 C/km per latest forecast soundings and analyses, and a dry layer near 500 mb noted in this morning's JAX sounding is supporting column theta-e deficits between 20-30 K. This thermodynamic profile is supportive of wet microbursts capable of damaging winds, and should persist for the next couple of hours until the air mass is overturned.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storms are likely to increase and coverage and intensity over the next few hours, with large damaging hail and wind gusts the most likely threats.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A cold front continues to push east across TX, now linking up with the east-west oriented boundary currently near Shreveport and extending eastward near I-20. Initial storms have shown signs of sporadic hail, but have been rather disorganized as they have remained north of the front. The air mass across the warm sector continues to destabilize, with MUCAPE now to 3000 J/kg. In addition, deep-layer shear remains quite favorable for organized convection capable damaging hail and wind gusts. Over the past 2 hours, GPS precipitable water sensors have shown a marked diurnal increase, related to the deepening boundary layer. This should aid new development along the intersecting frontal and outflow boundaries over northwest LA, with severe cells eventually progressing southeastward across LA later today. Farther east, another watch will likely be needed for the remainder of northern LA and extending into MS if storm coverage increases upstream and become severe. The instability-rich air mass and favorable flow regime would likely maintain the severe threat into the evening. ..Jewell.. 04/17/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The threat for damaging winds/hail continues for WW 136 as thunderstorms approach the I-35 corridor in south-central Texas.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Thunderstorms that have initiated along a cold front in south-central Texas have displayed organized mesocyclones at times, but have struggled to maintain intensity - likely due to lingering inhibition at around 850 mb that is noted in recent RAP mesoanalysis and forecast soundings. Despite this, the stratus that was in place ahead of these storms has begun to rapidly clear out as daytime heating drives deeper boundary-layer mixing. Latest forecasts suggest that any lingering capping will be overcome via mixing as temperatures approach the mid to upper 80s, which should be achievable in the next 1-2 hours. With surface dewpoints remaining in the upper 60s to low 70s, MLCAPE has increase to 2000-2500 J/kg, and regional VWPs continue to show strong flow above 5 km that is supporting nearly straight, elongated hodographs. As such, any storm that can persist until 21-23 UTC will likely see intensification and an increasing severe hail/wind threat. While exact timing and storm coverage remains uncertain, this intensification could occur as storms approach the higher population centers along the I-35 corridor. ..Moore.. 04/17/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A severe thunderstorm or two could produce large hail over the next few hours across parts of east TX. The overall threat is expected to remain conditional and isolated in time/space, precluding watch issuance.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Isolated convection has developed this afternoon near the I-45 corridor in Leon County TX. This activity is just ahead of a surface boundary draped across central into northeast TX. Temperatures have warmed into the mid 80s ahead of of these isolated cells, with dewpoints near 70 F. As a result, MLCAPE has increased to around 2000-2500 J/kg amid modest midlevel lapse rates. A broad agitated cumulus field is noted in visible satellite imagery as of 2115z, and at least one or two sustained storms could emerge from this area. However, current radar trends indicate convection is weakening and struggling to maintain intensity. Nevertheless, strong vertical shear resides across the region, with effective shear magnitudes near 40-45 kt. RAP and HRRR forecast soundings indicate little inhibition while hodographs are straight and elongated. Given strong instability and favorable shear profiles that would typically support rotating updrafts capable of large hail, a conditional threat for a severe storm or two will exist over the next few hours. Large-scale ascent will remain weak across the region, and convergence along the surface boundary is not as apparent as further southwest where supercells have produced significant hail this afternoon. Nevertheless, the environmental parameter space is sufficient for an organized supercell capable of large hail, should a cell become sustained. Given the the conditional and isolated nature of the threat, a watch is not expected at this time.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated large hail and locally strong wind gusts will be possible during the next couple hours across portions of the FL Panhandle and southern GA. Watch issuance is not expected at this time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Latest mosaic radar imagery shows a few strong updrafts embedded in a larger area of stratiform rain over the FL Panhandle into far southern GA. Steep low-level lapse rates and modest boundary-layer moisture (dewpoints in the middle 60s) are contributing to 1500 J/kg MLCAPE where VWPs show 35-45 knots 0-6km bulk shear. While low-level flow remains weak and large-scale ascent is minimal, steep midlevel lapse rates combined with the favorable mid/upper-level flow will continue to support isolated large hail with the stronger/persistent cores. Locally strong wind gusts will also be possible, mainly aided by precipitation loading and localized upscale growth. Watch issuance is not expected at this time.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Large hail will remain possible another couple of hours with strong to severe thunderstorms tracking south/southeast across parts of south-central TX.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A few strong to severe cells continue to spread south/southeast to the west of San Antonio. These cells are developing along a dryline and accessing surface dewpoints in the upper 60s to low 70s F and MLCAPE around 2000-2500 J/kg. Low-level shear remains weak across the region, with EWX VWP data indicating 15 kt or less westerly winds through 3 km. Nevertheless, wind speeds increase rapidly above 3 km, and effective shear magnitudes greater than 45 kt is supporting at least briefly organized cells. Elongated hodographs will continue to favor cells capable of large hail. MLCIN increases with south and east extent, but a corridor from Uvalde and Zavala Counties eastward across Frio and Atascosa may continue to see a threat (in addition to Bexar and Medina Counties) over the next couple of hours, and a local watch extension has been made across these counties by WFO EWX. ..Leitman.. 04/17/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe weather threat continues across WWs 135 and 137. Monitoring areas farther south in southern LA for new watch issuance later this evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A mix of discrete supercells and organized multi-cell clusters are advancing east-southeastward across northern LA and southern MS, where there have been multiple reports of large to very large hail. Within the inflow region of this convection, dewpoints in the upper 60s to lower 70s and steep low-level lapse rates are supporting 2000-2500 J/kg MLCAPE. In addition, the latest observations show surface pressure falls over southern MS, resulting in backed surface winds and associated increases in low-level SRH (around 200 m^2/s^2 0-1km SRH per DGX VWP). This enhanced low-level SRH, combined with favorable deep-layer shear (effective bulk shear near 45-55 knots) will continue to support supercells with a risk of large hail, damaging wind gusts, and perhaps a tornado or two. Eventually, convection should grow upscale and continue spreading southward into southern LA, where a new watch may eventually be needed. ..Weinman.. 04/17/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The risk of damaging outflow winds will continue spreading southward across southeastern LA, southern MS, and southwestern AL this evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Latest mosaic radar imagery shows an organizing MCS moving southward across southern MS, while a few supercell structures remain evident along the leading edge of the outflow boundary. South of the MCS, light southerly winds and dewpoints in the upper 60s/lower 70s will continue to support surface-based inflow, while the MOB VWP shows 0-6km bulk shear of 50 knots. Generally deep westerly flow parallel to the leading edge gust front of the MCS should continue to favor upscale growth and a primary risk of damaging outflow winds. However, any north-south oriented segments of the line could favor a localized risk of a brief embedded tornado owing to favorable low-level shear near 30 knots. ..Weinman.. 04/18/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Sporadic strong/locally damaging gusts and perhaps a tornado will be possible the next 1-2 hours. However, a gradual weakening trend is expected with eastward extent across southern AL into the FL Panhandle.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A QLCS across southwest AL into far southern MS will continue to shift east/southeast around 40-50 kt over the next few hours, mainly posing a threat for sporadic strong gusts. The line of convection is expected to approach the eastern edge of the watch by the 05z expiration time. Additionally, lead supercell just northeast of Mobile also may continue to pose a threat for hail and gusty winds in the near-term, though radar trends have indicated recent weakening. The downstream environment remains weakly unstable, though low-level inhibition is expected to continue to increase. Overall radar presentation of the QLCS has degraded over the past 15-30 minutes with the previously strong and tornadic bookend vortex diminishing. This suggests that the system is being impacted by the weaker downstream instability and increasing boundary-layer inhibition. VWP data from EVX and EOX indicate weakening vertical shear with eastward extent as well, further hindering maintenance of a stronger QLCS with time. While a few strong gusts and perhaps a tornado may be possible in the near-term, the overall threat is expected to gradually diminish with eastward extent. As such, a new watch is not expected downstream from WW 138 at this time. ..Leitman.. 04/18/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...
